questions.worked_solution:
Let $C={C}_{1}\cup {C}_{2}$ be a piecewise smooth path in the $xy$-plane, and let $-C$ be the curve consisting of the same points as $C$ but with the opposite orientation. 

For line integrals with respect to $y,$ we have the following properties:

- ${\int }_{-C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y=-{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y$

- ${\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y={\int }_{{C}_{1}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{{C}_{1}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y \\  & =-{\int }_{-{C}_{1}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y \\  & =-3+5 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculate ${\int }_{C}\,\text{d}x,$ where $C$ is the path along a quarter circle of radius $3,$ traversed from the point $(1,-3)$ to the point $(4,0),$ shown above.
questions.worked_solution:
The line integral of unity with respect to $x$ along a path $C$ is equal to the net change in $x$ between the terminal and initial points:

$$
{\int }_{C}\,\text{d}x={x}_{2}-{x}_{1},
$$

where ${x}_{2}$ is the $x$-coordinate of the terminal point, and ${x}_{1}$ is the $x$-coordinate of the initial point.

In our case, ${x}_{2}=4$ and ${x}_{1}=1.$ Therefore,

$$
{\int }_{C}\,\text{d}x={x}_{2}-{x}_{1}=4-1=3.
$$

The line integral of unity with respect to $x$ along a path $C$ is equal to the net change in $x$ between the terminal and initial points:

$$
{∮}_{C}\,\text{d}x={x}_{2}-{x}_{1},
$$

where ${x}_{2}$ is the $x$-coordinate of the terminal point, and ${x}_{1}$ is the $x$-coordinate of the initial point.

In our case, the initial and terminal points are the same (since the path is closed and is traversed only once). Therefore, ${x}_{1}={x}_{2},$ and we have

$$
{∮}_{C}\,\text{d}x=0.
$$
